name: Window Control
description:
List, move and tile windows from a script, a rules file or the keyboard. It works on Wayland, where wmctrl and xdotool reach only XWayland windows.

* Scripts: list every window with its ID, title, WM class, PID, workspace, monitor and geometry. Activate, move, resize, minimize, maximize, fullscreen, keep above, make sticky or close a window, move it to another workspace or monitor, or wait until a window opens. Use the wctl command-line client or any D-Bus client, such as gdbus.
* Rules: a rule in ~/.config/gnome-window-control/rules.json places a matching window when it opens. The preferences window has an editor for the file that checks each rule as you type.
* Keyboard: Super+Ctrl and a numpad key tile the focused window on a 4x2 grid. Super+Ctrl and the numpad * applies the rules again. You can rebind or unbind every shortcut in the preferences window.

An optional top-bar icon applies the rules again and opens the preferences window. When you disable the extension, the D-Bus interface, the rules, the shortcuts and the icon stop.

IMPORTANT: the D-Bus interface has no access control. Any application in your session can read your window titles and control your windows, also while the screen is locked. Do not enable the extension if that is not acceptable to you.

wctl is a separate download and is not installed with this extension. Get it and the full documentation from the project page.
